target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (T : ArithmeticTheory) (σ : ArithmeticSentence), Def3 T → Def2 σ → Def3 (T ∪ {σ}).theory
translation: Target is the proposition that for every set T of arithmetic sentences (an arbitrary arithmetic theory, with no further assumptions such as recursive enumerability or deductive closure) and every arithmetic sentence σ, if every sentence in T is true in the standard model of arithmetic (the natural numbers) and σ is true in the standard model of arithmetic, then every arithmetic sentence derivable in classical first-order logic from the axiom set T ∪ {σ} is true in the standard model of arithmetic.

divergences.description: The parenthetical states a general principle about any sound system and any true statement (which the surrounding passage applies to the non-arithmetical assumption 'I am F'), whereas the Lean target specializes it to first-order arithmetic theories (in ℒₒᵣ), arithmetic sentences, truth in the standard model ℕ, and classical first-order deduction (which also builds in truth-preserving inference rules).

In the source, 'system' refers to a formal (recursively enumerable) system, whereas the target quantifies over arbitrary sets T of arithmetic sentences without requiring T.RE (a harmless strengthening of the hypothesis) and does not explicitly state in the conclusion that the supplemented system remains recursively enumerable.

The hypothesis assumes soundness of the axiom set T (Def3 T) while the conclusion asserts soundness of the deductive closure (Def3 (T ∪ {σ}).theory); under classical first-order logic Def3 T is equivalent to Def3 T.theory, so this is a presentational difference.

judgement.summary: The Lean statement faithfully captures the parenthetical's logical content—adding a true sentence to a sound theory preserves soundness of all derived theorems—specialized to classical first-order arithmetic theories and standard-model truth without tracking recursive enumerability.
